title: Only a messenger
hookLine: Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers passed before him (3:144)

lines: IF HE WAS GONE, WHAT WAS LEFT?
cards: In the chaos at Uhud, someone shouted that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ had been killed. He hadn't; he was wounded, and his companions closed around him. But the rumor ran through the army faster than the truth.
Some men put down their swords and sat. Some started thinking about running. If he was gone, what was left?
The commentators say a verse came down about that moment. And years later, on the day he really did die, someone stood up and read it aloud.

teach.b: In Pickthall's words: "Muhammad is but a messenger, messengers (the like of whom) have passed away before him." Then it asks: if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?

Whoever turns back doesn't harm God at all. A startling verse to find in scripture: a plain statement that the Prophet is mortal, and that faith isn't meant to hang on one human life. Now the second scene.
Medina, years later. The Prophet has died in the room of his wife A'ishah. Umar, a companion known for his strength, can't accept it; he stands in the mosque insisting it isn't true.
Then Abu Bakr arrives, the Prophet's close friend and companion. He goes in, uncovers the Prophet's face, and kisses him. Then he comes out to the crowd.

teach.h: GOD IS ALIVE AND DOES NOT DIE
teach.b: According to the account in Sahih al-Bukhari, he says: whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died; and whoever worships God, God is alive and does not die. And he recites 3:144.
The report says it was as if people had never heard the verse before, and then everyone was reciting it. Umar said his legs gave way when he heard it.
A hadith in Bukhari ties faith to loving the Prophet more than one's own parent and child.
And still the Qur'an itself says he was a man, a messenger, one in a long line. What he brought, the prayer, the Qur'an, the way of living, is meant to keep going after him.

how: Muslims honor the Prophet as the final messenger while holding that he was a mortal man; 3:144 and Abu Bakr's words at his death are often recalled when teaching that faith rests on God, not on any person.

games.q: you're Abu Bakr. the Prophet has died, and Umar is telling the crowd it isn't true. what do you do?
o: agree with Umar to calm people.
say God is alive and does not die, and recite 3:144.
send everyone home and say nothing.
games.why: he told them whoever worshipped God, God is alive, and recited the verse. people said it was as if they had never heard it before.

practice: Think of someone who taught you something that mattered and is no longer in your life: a grandparent, a teacher, a friend who moved away, someone who died.
Instead of dwelling on the loss, ask what of theirs is still alive in you, a habit, a phrase, a way of treating people, and name it. If you pray, you can ask mercy for them.
